answer: An agent market funding raven surveys around a lagoon weights contract-allocation votes by tokens locked for 30 days, not by account count. Each vote carries a signal proportional to its locked stake, and the same tokens cannot back two votes. Splitting 100 tokens across a thousand fake agents therefore buys no more influence than one agent with 100 tokens. To gain influence, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, paying capital and liquidity costs.
